comment: P8 sink-surface waivers — each row is an ACCUSATION that a shipped engine violates the clause it cites, recorded by gen_sink_surface.py's FIRST run (2026-08-12) so the matrix lands green over defects it found rather than defects it ignores. The ratchet is both-ways: a waived cell that starts passing is STALE and fails the run, so no row outlives its defect.

§3.2 ⟨0.28⟩ 'the sinks named elsewhere in that argv are still sinks' + §3.3 'fail-closed document for EVERY cause' — `--target --gate-json -` exits 2 with NOTHING on the stream. The FILE spelling passes (the pre-pass leaves an armed placeholder on disk), so this is a refusal path that exits without routing through the stream emitter — the same class as the bare exit(2) candor-scan repaired in 3560681, one flag over. Found by this matrix's first run, 2026-08-12: the hand sweep had covered --policy and --out on this CLI, not --target.

§3.3: '--help / -h | print a usage summary that lists these flags' — the jar answers `verify --help` with a usage line carrying value-taking --run/--report/--scope, but the top-level --help never mentions the verb. An undisclosed flag surface, in the engine whose subject is disclosure. Found by this matrix's first run, 2026-08-12.

§3.3: the usage summary MUST list the flags — candor-java's query grammar ACCEPTS `--class` as a value-taking flag on every verb (it refuses it a value like a real flag: '--class was given no value'), but --help never documents it; candor-rust and candor-ts document theirs. Found by this matrix's first run, 2026-08-12.
